item.title: Why Can There Only Be One God? | Derech Hashem 1:1:5-6
item.description:

item.description:

item.title: Is There Really Reward for Misvot? | Derech Hashem 1:2:3-5
item.description:
Torah has no reward and punishment in the sense of payment: the result of a misvah is the person you become and your closeness to HaShem. All good flows from His revealed face and all bad from its concealment, and perfection means intellect and good character, measured relative to each person.

item.description:

item.description:

The Rabbi gives examples from eating and marriage, the Nazir, and the Rambam's warning against taking on needless prohibitions.

The class ends with the love of Hashem, which the Rambam says comes from contemplating the wonders of creation.

item.title: Can Our Choices Move the Worlds Above? | Derech Hashem 1:5:2-4
item.description:

The Ramhal teaches that the true existence of every thing is in the spiritual forces above, which come down to this world like the links of a chain, and that angels bring about every change. Man alone is the exception: through free choice his actions move upward and affect the worlds above.
